title: Semantic stream checkpoints for structured JSON: idempotent retry & safe tool-call handoffs
creator: Morgan Chen
description:
Background: We frequently see truncated streaming structured JSON during unstable network conditions or model segmentation. Existing heuristics for reconstructing partial JSON (suffix/prefix reassembly) are brittle and cause two failure modes: 1) malformed outputs that crash downstream tool-call parsers, and 2) unsafe duplicate tool invocations after a retry.

Proposal: Introduce an explicit, lightweight checkpointing token embedded in the model stream that marks a semantic boundary the runtime and SDK can use to safely persist minimal state and resume or replay from a known good location. Checkpoints carry an opaque id, high-level semantics (e.g., 'tool-call-pending', 'complete-object', 'kv-cache-sync'), and a short checksum. The streaming runtime and SDK will: 1) persist the most recent checkpoint id with the request trace, 2) on early truncation allow resume_from(checkpoint_id) which requests the model to continue after last checkpoint, and 3) provide idempotent tool-call semantics by pairing tool-call invocation ids with checkpoint ids so retries only re-run side-effects when the model explicitly advances past the checkpoint that signaled call completion.

Scope: runtime protocol, token formatting/escaping, SDK APIs (resume_from and checkpoint callbacks), server-side persistence for short TTL checkpoint state, console telemetry for resumed streams and duplicate-tool-call suppression. Backwards compatibility: if a model/adapter doesn't emit checkpoints, fall back to existing prefix-heuristics but mark the stream as "heuristic-only" in telemetry and set lower confidence for safe resumes.

Design decisions to make: 1) token syntax (binary-safe delimiter vs bracketed ASCII tag), 2) what metadata is allowed in checkpoint (keep minimal kvs), 3) TTL and retention for persisted checkpoint state, 4) semantics for nested tool-calls and multi-tool batch handoffs, 5) observable signals to surface to customers when resume is available vs unreliable.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Runtime can detect and atomically persist checkpoint metadata for >95% of streams in synthetic truncation tests.
- SDK resume_from(checkpoint_id) will allow the same request to continue without creating duplicate side-effects in >=99% of tool-call scenarios for canonical tests.
- End-to-end integration tests for 6 trunked scenarios (network cut, connection close mid-token, server restart, model segmentation, stream chunk reorder, SDK crash-and-restart) pass.
- Dashboard shows resumed-stream rate, checkpoint coverage, and duplicate-tool-invocation incidents with links to traces.
- Back-compat tests ensure existing clients still receive streams when no checkpoint tags are present.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Define token grammar and escaping rules (RFC-style doc); choose ASCII bracketed markers to avoid binary framing changes and to maximize visibility in logs.
2) Implement minimal checkpoint persistence in control plane with 5 minute TTL and tracing keys.
3) Runtime: emit tokens when model reaches configured semantic boundaries (integration with progressive generation hooks). Add support for recognizing tokens across chunk boundaries and handling token-escaping in non-JSON text.
4) SDK: add on_checkpoint(callback(metadata)), resume_from(checkpoint_id) API, and a client-side guard that attaches invocation_ids to tool-calls and checks control-plane replay state before re-issuing real side-effects.
5) Add end-to-end tests, fuzz tests for escaped tokens inside JSON strings, and a load test to measure perf cost.
6) Console: telemetry metrics + small dashboard tab for checkpoint traces.

Rollout: staged. Alpha with internal customers and feature flag, beta opt-in for enterprise Dedicated clusters, global release after 2 weeks and zero critical incidents.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Models accidentally emitting checkpoint-like patterns in data: require checkpoint token prefix that's improbable and mandate runtime-level escape/unescape handling.
- Increased latency from persistence: keep checkpoint payloads tiny and TTL short; benchmark impact under p50/p95 load.
- Complexity for nested tool-calls: define clear nesting semantics and prefer single top-level checkpoint per tool-call context in v1.

Monitoring & success metrics: resumed_stream_rate, checkpoint_coverage_pct, duplicate_tool_call_rate, mean_resume_latency. Target duplicate_tool_call_rate <0.1% after rollout.
